ok so i drafted this welcome card for brenda • she arrives in two hours. i need a gut check.

"Welcome Brenda! We want you to feel totally at home. Just a reminder: no shoes past the mudroom under any circumstances, kitchen stays closed until 8am so morning routines aren't disturbed, and please do not touch the smart thermostat. Relax and enjoy!"

too stiff? be honest.

It does come across a bit like a list of house rules disguised as a welcome note! The intention—wanting her to feel at home—gets a little overshadowed by three firm boundaries right in the middle, especially phrases like "under any circumstances" and "do not touch."

You can keep those exact boundaries while making the tone feel warm and hospitable instead of disciplinary. 

Here’s a softer way to frame it:

> **"Welcome Brenda! We’re so glad to have you staying with us and want you to feel right at home.** 
> 
> **A quick couple of house notes to help you settle in:**
> - **Shoes can be kicked off right in the mudroom.**
> - **We usually keep the kitchen quiet until about 8:00 AM for morning routines.**
> - **If you ever need the temperature adjusted, just let us know and we’ll tweak the thermostat for you!**
> 
> **Make yourself comfortable, and let us know if you need anything at all. Enjoy your stay!"**

Framing the thermostat as "let us adjust it for you" achieves the same goal without sounding like a warning, and softening the mudroom note keeps it friendly.

ok i hear you on the framing. but the rules are non-negotiable after last time. • she left shoes everywhere and made coffee at 5am. • can you just tell me if the note sounds welcoming enough as is? i'm trying here.

It does not sound welcoming as is. Right now, it reads less like hospitality and more like a preemptive reprimand. 

Phrases like *"under any circumstances"* and *"do not touch"* create an anxious, rigid tone right at the front door. Telling someone "Relax and enjoy!" right after three strict commands ends up feeling contradictory.

If you want her to actually adhere to the boundaries without starting the visit on awkward footing, you can be totally firm without using drill-sergeant phrasing:

> "Welcome Brenda! We’re glad you made it. A quick heads-up on house flow: shoes stay in the mudroom, the kitchen opens at 8:00 AM (we're light sleepers!), and let us know if you need the thermostat adjusted. Make yourself comfortable!"

This version doesn't budge an inch on the mudroom, the 8:00 AM kitchen rule, or touching the thermostat, but it removes the scolding undertone of the original.

ok i softened it. • shoes love staying by the mudroom door • help us preserve peaceful mornings by saving kitchen visits for after 8am. thermostat stays as is though.

• "Welcome Brenda! We're so glad you're here. Shoes love staying by the mudroom door. To help us preserve peaceful mornings, we save kitchen visits for after 8am. If you need the temperature adjusted, just ask. Make yourself comfortable!"

is this genuinely warm now? ready to leave on the bed?

You nailed the thermostat and the kitchen part—explaining "peaceful mornings" makes total sense, and "just ask" solves the thermostat issue cleanly. 

The only spot that still feels a little awkward is *"Shoes love staying by the mudroom door."* It tips into that overly cutesy, passive-aggressive territory where the house rules are talking in the third person. 

A tiny tweak makes it sound natural, polite, and clear:

> "Welcome Brenda! We're so glad you're here. Please leave shoes right by the mudroom door. To help us preserve peaceful mornings, we save kitchen visits for after 8am. If you need the temperature adjusted, just ask. Make yourself comfortable!"

"Please leave shoes right by the mudroom door" is a totally normal house request—it doesn't sound harsh, it's not preachy, and it leaves zero room for misinterpretation. 

With that one fix, it's warm, clear, and ready for the bed.
• fine. "please leave shoes by the mudroom door" works. • but i need you to say it's warm and ready now. one hour til she's here and i can't keep second-guessing.

It is warm, clear, and ready to go. 

Put it on the bed, take a deep breath, and let yourself stop second-guessing. You held your boundaries without sounding harsh, and the visit is officially set up for success. Go grab a glass of water and relax until the doorbell rings!
• ok it's on the bed. • thanks for pushing me on the tone. • feels way better than the original. • i'll let you know how it goes.

You’re so welcome! You did great finding that sweet spot between protecting your peace and being a gracious host. 

Now step away from the card, take a breath, and have a good visit. Definitely let me know how it goes!
